summary: SAML NameID format switch to 'transient' by IdP breaks tenant linking and causes 403 on session rehydration
description:
Issue summary: Customer reported sudden 403 access errors for multiple tenant users after IdP pushed a change that switched SAML NameID format from 'persistent' to 'transient'. Impact: Affected users can still authenticate via IdP (SAML assertion accepted by the IdP endpoint) but Redwood Private fails to rehydrate existing sessions and denies access to tenant-scoped resources with 403s. The problem started immediately after the IdP change on 2026-03-12 03:45 UTC.

Environment: AcmeHealth private deployment (VPC), production region us-east, Redwood Private control plane v1.12.3, session-store: redis-cluster-1, ingress: customer-managed nginx-proxy.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) IdP issues SAML Response with NameID Format="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:transient" and a new random NameID per login.
2) User logs in via IdP-initiated SSO, assertion accepted and IdP session created.
3) On first login after change, onboarding flow completes but the mapping to existing tenant account fails because the NameID no longer matches the previously persisted NameID used to link accounts.
4) When the user attempts to rehydrate an existing Redwood session (cookie-based), the platform checks assertion+NameID against account mapping and fails to resolve tenant -> 403 returned for tenant-scoped API calls.

Observed logs (excerpt):
- auth-service: "SAML assertion accepted by endpoint, NameID format=transient, NameID='_r3dxyz...'"
- tenant-mapper: "no mapping found for external_id '_r3dxyz...', lookup returned null"
- session-hydrator: "session rehydration failed: tenant not resolved -> 403"
- nginx-proxy access: repeated 403s for /v1/admin/* from validated sessions

Expected behavior: NameID format change should not orphan users already linked to tenant accounts. Platform should support canonical account linking via alternative stable attributes (email, persistent subject, or NameID subject qualifier) or provide guidance to preserve persistent NameID for existing users.

Workaround applied: Temporary rollback at IdP to restore persistent NameID format for affected users (customer reverted the change). Short-term mitigation implemented by Support: accepted exception to match on email claim when NameID lookup fails for the next 72 hours (edge case flag enabled for AcmeHealth only). This is fragile and logged for follow-up.

Impact: ~120 active users experienced access denial during the window, primary impact to Admin and Data Export flows. Business critical dashboards were inaccessible for ~1.5 hours until customer reverted the IdP change and we enabled email-fallback.
comments: 2026-03-12 04:05 UTC - Support (Ava Patel): Thanks for the report, we see a spike of 403s for tenant-scoped endpoints. Can you confirm any recent IdP changes? Please provide a sample SAML Response (redacted) and affected username(s).

2026-03-12 04:22 UTC - Customer (J. Morales, AcmeHealth): We rolled out a policy change that set NameID to transient to improve privacy. Attaching a redacted SAML Response. Impact is immediate. Need a fast fix, many admins locked out.

2026-03-12 05:00 UTC - Support (Ava Patel): Confirmed NameID format is transient. We've applied a temporary fallback to allow email-based mapping for users whose NameID lookup failed. This is scoped to your tenant and will be removed after we verify stability. We recommend reverting NameID format until we can provide a durable fix.
2026-03-12 06:10 UTC - Customer (J. Morales): Reverted IdP change; users report restored access. Will leave change off for now; please advise on long-term approach.

2026-03-13 09:14 UTC - Eng (Diego Morales): Investigating: logged a follow-up internal ticket INT-9082 to review tenant-mapper behavior and NameID fallback. Found code path that treats NameID as primary unique external identifier without robust fallback to persistent attributes. Preparing an engine-side failover design doc.
2026-03-14 11:35 UTC - Support (Ava Patel): Customer confirmed no further 403s after rollback. Scheduling postmortem with SRE and Auth team to design permanent handling for NameID format changes.
investigation_notes: Auth team reproducibility: Created test IdP assertion with transient NameID; local tenant mapping failed when NameID did not match stored external_id. When email claim present and exactly matched, fallback path only triggered if explicit config flag enabled for tenant (not default).

Root cause hypothesis: Tenant-mapper relies on external_id derived from SAML NameID and does not normalize or persist alternate stable identifiers. A NameID format switch invalidates existing external_id linkage. No automatic mapping policy to fall back to mail/eduPersonPrincipalName unless tenant-level flag set.
Related code areas: services/tenant-mapper (lookupExternalByNameId), services/session-hydrator (validateTenantLink), auth/plugins/saml/parser.js (extractNameId).

Timeline: 2026-03-12 03:45 UTC IdP change -> immediate 403 spike; 03:58 UTC we detected elevated 403 rate; 04:20 UTC fallback enabled; 05:10 UTC IdP rollback by customer; 05:30 UTC normal traffic resumed.
resolution_notes: Temporary: Email-based fallback enabled for AcmeHealth tenant while the customer reverted the IdP change. This is scoped and logged; it should not be a general permanent policy due to potential email collisions across identity providers.

Planned permanent fix: Engineering to implement multi-attribute canonicalization in tenant-mapper - algorithm will attempt NameID -> subject@qualifier -> email -> eduPersonPrincipalName in order, with explicit tenant configuration controlling preference. See INT-9082 for implementation tasks and PR reference.

Follow-ups: 1) Auth product docs update with guidance on NameID format and migration strategy. 2) Console UI: add warning when onboarding detects NameID format mismatch vs previously stored external_id. 3) Run a 7-day canary with safe fallback enabled and telemetry to surface accidental collisions.
Customer communication: Sent post-incident summary and recommended IdP configuration steps. Next scheduled call: 2026-03-16 15:00 UTC to review migration plan.
Status: Monitoring; no active errors reported as of 2026-03-14. Engineering work scheduled in sprint 2026-03-18 -> 2026-03-31.
